requirements.note: One long feed, newest first. Each post shows author, handle and relative time ('16m ago'), the full text, a full-width image with rounded corners at its own aspect ratio, and a horizontally scrolling carousel of image cards with titles. Carousel images are cropped, not distorted.
The heart toggles to a filled red heart and the count changes 872→873 and back. The reply count shows as 'N replies'.

Tapping a post pushes a 'Post' screen with an edge-to-edge (larger) image. Tapping an image, in the feed, in the detail screen or on a carousel card, opens a black full-screen viewer that closes with a swipe down.
Pull to refresh adds three made-up posts at the top (Sam Rivera, Leo Martin, Maya Chen, 'just now'). There is also a refresh button in the nav bar.
The compose button opens a sheet with Cancel / New Post / Post. The keyboard comes up on its own and Post stays disabled until there is text. The new post appears at the top as 'You @you · just now'.
After relaunch the like (873, filled) is kept, along with the composed post and the refreshed posts.

tells: At the largest text size the avatar turns from a circle into a large rounded square stacked above the name, which looks odd.
When scrolled at large text, the small inline 'Feed' title sits on top of post text under the glass bar and is hard to read.
The full-screen viewer's close button is a dark rounded square, not a circular glass button, and the status bar stays visible over the photo.
The composer's 'YO' initials avatar for 'You' looks auto-generated.
Full-screen viewer has no pinch-to-zoom affordance and does not let you page through a carousel's cards.
A.scroll: Smooth on slow drags and flings, with no blank rows or pop-in. Images are present on arrival, and scroll position is kept when returning from a post. The large title collapses into a glass inline bar as on iOS 26+.

requirements.note: Newest-first feed of cards with author, handle, relative time ('16m'), full text and rounded full-width images at the correct aspect. Carousels ('9 moments' with titled cards) scroll horizontally, but many card images are visibly stretched: circular suns render as ovals.
The heart toggles filled and the count changes 872↔873. The reply count is shown as a bubble with a number.

Tapping a post pushes a 'Moment' screen with a slightly larger image (382 vs 338 pt wide) and a full timestamp. Tapping an image or a carousel card opens a full-screen black viewer with a caption and 'Swipe down to close'. A swipe down closes it.
Pull to refresh adds three made-up posts at the top and shows a '3 new moments' pill.
The orange compose button opens a 'New moment' sheet with a placeholder. The keyboard comes up on its own and Post is disabled until there is text. The post appears at the top.
After relaunch the like, the composed post and the refreshed posts are all kept.

bugs: Carousel card images are distorted (aspect ratio not kept): round suns show as ovals in many cards, e.g. Chili Cauliflower, Coconut Tofu and Spiced Gnocchi.
tells: No large title. The nav bar is a custom serif 'Feed' wordmark with a sun icon, and it does not grow with Dynamic Type.
The nav bar is an opaque flat bar that cuts content off hard, with no glass or scroll-edge blur.
The compose button is a hand-styled solid orange circle, not a system bar button.
A marketing-style hero header ('LIFE, AS IT HAPPENS / Small moments. Good company.') sits at the top of the feed, which reads more like a web landing page than an iOS app.
Posts are rounded cards on a beige background, a custom look rather than the iOS list style.
At the largest text size, avatars shrink to tiny circles beside huge names, the eyebrow's dot no longer lines up with its text, and the handle and time wrap.
The full-screen viewer's 'Swipe down to close' hint text is non-standard.
B.scroll: Smooth on drags and flings, with no blank cards or pop-in. Scroll position is kept when returning from a post. The carousel scrolls horizontally with a peek of the next card.

why: Both apps meet every requirement and keep likes and posts across relaunch. B, however, stretches its carousel images. A also looks and behaves like a stock iOS 26 app: large title collapsing into a glass bar, system toolbar buttons and a plain list. B's custom branded chrome, opaque bar and hero header make it feel less native, and its layout copes less well at the largest text size.
